clue.text: Pale food

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a pastry case filled with meat and vegetables

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a menu note, but each is a separate meaning of one word. A Cornish pasty is a British baked pastry turnover.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a sallow complexion, and the noun names a folded savoury pastry.

clue.text: River bird bathing leg, preening type

indicators.note: bathing means the river and bird wrap round the leg, as water surrounds a bather

parts.note: the PO is the river of northern Italy
a JAY is a bird
PIN is slang for a leg

explanation.surface: A bird in the river, washing its leg and preening.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a bird washing in the river, but the river and the bird are separate pieces, and 'leg' is slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A popinjay is a vain, conceited person, fond of showing off.

clue.text: Stew provided to feed variety of toads

indicators.note: to feed means the condition word is put inside the rearranged letters
variety of suggests a different form of the letters of toads

parts.note: IF means provided that

explanation.surface: A stew made to feed several kinds of toad.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging TOADS gives STADO, and IF goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stifado is a Greek beef and onion casserole.

clue.text: I've got it after you before, all right!

indicators.note: after places the realisation cry following the old word for you

parts.note: YE is how 'you' was said in earlier times
AH is a cry of realisation

explanation.surface: Someone realises they've understood, following someone else, and agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeah is casual speech for yes, signalling agreement like all right.

clue.text: Fuel smell recalled by soldier

parts.note: a PARA is a paratrooper

indicators.note: recalled, read as called back, has the smell word run from its end to its start

parts.note: NIFF is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A soldier remembers the whiff of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the pieces side by side. The smell word is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is kerosene, an oil burnt in lamps and heaters.

clue.text: Complete swine in cad: sort she messed around

indicators.note: in puts the pig inside the jumbled letters
messed around shows those letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: a BOAR is a male pig

explanation.surface: A scoundrel of a pig, with a woman fooling around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete swine' reads as one insult, but 'Complete' is the definition. The anagram of CAD SORT SHE gives ACROSSTHED, with BOAR going in.
explanation.definitionFit: Across-the-board means applying to everyone or everything, so total or universal.

clue.text: Passionate singer uplifted

indicators.note: uplifted, in a down clue, has the singer word read from bottom to top

parts.note: a DIVA is a celebrated female singer

explanation.surface: A passionate singer raised to new heights.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen or eager, showing great enthusiasm.

clue.text: Very hot month set one's teeth on edge

parts.note: FEB is the calendar abbreviation for February
to RILE is to irritate, to set one's teeth on edge

explanation.surface: A sweltering month that really grates.
explanation.definitionFit: Febrile means feverish, having a high temperature.

clue.text: Leader of revolution has abandoned country? You're kidding!

indicators.note: has abandoned means that first letter leaves the country word

parts.note: NORWAY is a country

indicators.note: Leader of picks the first letter of revolution

explanation.surface: A revolutionary leader has fled the country, which seems unbelievable.
explanation.definitionFit: No way is an exclamation of disbelief, like saying surely not.

clue.text: Drink whiskey and rum this Noel: sweet!

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the following letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Christmas drinks of whisky and rum, which taste sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whiskey' and 'rum' look like spirits but are a letter and the anagram signal. Rearranging THIS NOEL SWEET gives ETONESWHISTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wet one's whistle is an idiom for having a drink.

clue.text: Man, say, bound to cut head

indicators.note: to cut means the boundary word slices into the head word, sitting inside it

parts.note: PATE is an old word for the head
a bound is a boundary or edge, a RIM

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to lop off a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' reads as 'obliged to', but 'bound' is the noun for an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans are an example of the primates, the order of mammals including apes and monkeys.

clue.text: Line bags in black alongside a colourful array

indicators.note: bags means grabs and holds, so the line word wraps the other letters

parts.note: a line of things is a ROW

indicators.note: alongside sets the A right beside the IN and B, before them

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A line stuffs things into black beside something brightly coloured.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes alongside IN and B to make AINB, which ROW then bags.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is the arc of spectrum colours seen when sunlight passes through rain.

clue.text: Current shift in the Calcutta Cup, last of all

indicators.note: last of all asks for the final letter of every one of the four words

explanation.surface: Something changes now in the Calcutta Cup, the England v Scotland rugby trophy, right at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The Calcutta Cup is the annual rugby union trophy played for by England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A neap is a tide of small range, so it is a movement of tidal water.

clue.text: Crow flies, finally, into vessel

indicators.note: into puts that letter inside the vessel word

parts.note: a BOAT is a vessel

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of flies

explanation.surface: A crow flies at last into a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird but is the verb for bragging.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag loudly about one's success.

clue.text: A little moment in year, minute

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A brief instant in the course of a year lasts only a minute.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, pronounced my-NEWT, is an adjective meaning extremely small.

clue.text: Primarily diabolical and wicked — am I?

definitions.text: Primarily diabolical and wicked — am I?

indicators.note: Primarily picks the first letter of diabolical

parts.note: wicked means EVIL

explanation.surface: Something diabolical and wicked asks whether it is the one meant.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil is fiendish and wicked by nature, the embodiment of evil.

clue.text: Place where infant goes crazy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a child's chamber pot
second meaning: British informal for mad or silly

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both a toddler's toilet and a casual word for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a small child's toilet bowl, and the adjective means foolish or mad.

clue.text: Bosses introduced to fresh idea not previously communicated

indicators.note: introduced to means the bosses are put into the middle of the rearranged letters
fresh says these letters are made anew in a different order

parts.note: FOREMEN are workplace bosses

explanation.surface: Managers are presented with a new idea nobody had mentioned before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not previously communicated' looks like the definition of something new, but 'not' belongs to the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforementioned means already mentioned or referred to earlier.

clue.text: Sign coat damaged? I'm sceptical

definitions.note: the definition is what such a person would say, describing them

indicators.note: damaged means the letters are broken up and put back differently

explanation.surface: A sign painted on a coat is damaged, and someone doubts it.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic doubts that God's existence can be known, a sceptic about belief.

clue.text: Sport in which participants struggle, grappling with tiredness?

parts.note: ALL IN means exhausted, here standing for the state of tiredness
WRESTLING is grappling with an opponent

explanation.surface: A sport where people wrestle, fighting their own fatigue.
explanation.walkthrough: All-in wrestling is a free-style form with few holds barred; 'all in' also means worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of the combat sport has two people grappling to pin each other down.

clue.text: Apprentice runs into Tower of Pisa, possibly?

indicators.note: into puts the runs letter inside the word for something that leans

parts.note: the Leaning Tower is one example of something that leans, a LEANER
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A trainee runs into the Leaning Tower of Pisa.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone still being taught a skill, like a trainee.

clue.text: Rush, perhaps to welcome queen from Shiraz?

indicators.note: to welcome means the footballer's name takes the queen into its middle

parts.note: Ian Rush was the Liverpool and Wales footballer, giving his first name IAN
a RANI is a Hindu queen

explanation.surface: A rush to greet a queen arriving from Shiraz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like haste but is the footballer Ian Rush. Shiraz is a city in Iran, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiraz is a city in Iran, so a person or thing from there is of that country.

clue.text: Finish off ham, then finish off lamb, say?

indicators.note: Finish off picks the final letter of ham

parts.note: to finish off a meal is to EAT it up

explanation.surface: Polish off the ham, and then the lamb too.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase does two jobs: first it takes the end of 'ham', then it means consume.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb is one example of flesh eaten as food.

clue.text: Second baby, clean

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second
a PUP is a baby animal

explanation.surface: A second baby to wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to wipe away spills, making a surface spotless.

clue.text: Grape for pruning back

indicators.note: back has those words read from the end to the start

parts.note: something for pruning is used TO NIP shoots

explanation.surface: A grape variety suited to cutting back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pruning back' sounds like a gardening phrase, but 'back' acts on 'to nip'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot noir and pinot grigio are wine grape varieties.

clue.text: County viewed in cinema, Yorkshire

indicators.note: viewed in says the answer can be seen sitting within the next words

explanation.surface: A county seen on screen in a Yorkshire cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland, while Yorkshire is a county of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is one of the Irish counties, in the province of Connacht.

clue.text: Latest four points

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the most recent information
second meaning: North, East, West and South, the four compass points, by their initials

explanation.walkthrough: The compass points by their initials happen to spell the word for fresh reports.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means recent reports of events, and it is also the initials of the compass directions.

clue.text: Island capital short of a tree

indicators.note: short of means the island capital lacks the letter that follows

parts.note: PALMA is the capital of Majorca

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean island capital without a single tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm is a tropical tree with a crown of large fronds.

clue.text: Strong dope locked in boot

indicators.note: locked in means the information word is shut inside the kick word

parts.note: to boot a ball is to kick it, to PUNT
dope is inside information, GEN in British slang

explanation.surface: Potent drugs hidden in a car's boot.
explanation.walkthrough: The boot here is a kick, not the car's luggage space, and dope is information, not drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent smell or taste is sharp and powerful.

clue.text: Practical type, pugilist punching others

indicators.note: punching means the boxer breaks into the middle of the others word

parts.note: the REST means the others
Muhammad ALI was the famous boxer

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth boxer lays into everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is a person who accepts situations as they are and acts sensibly.

clue.text: Spirit abandoned, popped one's clogs

parts.note: a PERI is a fairy spirit of Persian legend
SHED means cast off or abandoned

explanation.surface: A ghost, deserted, has died.
explanation.walkthrough: To pop one's clogs is British slang for to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Popped one's clogs is a humorous British idiom for died.

clue.text: Very energetic citizen of English city briefly touring India

indicators.note: touring means the citizen word goes round the letter for India

parts.note: a MANC is short for a Mancunian, a person from Manchester
I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A lively Mancunian travelling round India.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes frantic, frenzied activity and excitement.
